questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT true about spinal muscular atrophy (SMA)?

There is currently a full cure for all patients.
It can affect muscles used for breathing and swallowing.

key_points: Researchers tested a spine-stimulating implant on three people with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), a genetic disease with no cure that destroys motor neurons and weakens muscles.
After using the implant with regular spinal stimulation, all three participants showed improved muscle strength and could walk farther in six minutes than before.
The improvements did not disappear immediately when the stimulator was turned off, but they decreased a few months after the study ended.
A researcher not involved in the study said it was an important but small, short test that should be tried on other muscle-degenerating diseases.
main_idea: A small study found that a spine-stimulating implant, already used to treat paralysis, temporarily improved muscle strength and walking ability in three patients with the genetic disease SMA.
restate_sentence: They implanted electrodes over the lower spinal cord of the three adults with SMA.
